cues.en: November

saw one of the most widespread power outages in North American history. On the freezing cold evening of the ninth, the grid was operating at maximum capacity as people tried to stay warm when a misconfigured relay tripped a breaker on a key transmission line. The loss of that single line cascaded into a loss of service for over 30,000,000
cues.zh: 发生了北美历史上规模最大的停电之一。9日那个寒冷的夜晚，电网正满负荷运转，人们都想取暖，这时一个配置错误的继电器跳开了一条关键输电线路上的断路器。仅仅这一条线路的损失，就连锁导致美国东北部以及安大略和加拿大部分地区超过3000万人

cues.en: people in the Northeast US plus parts of Ontario and Canada. Restoring electricity to that many people is no simple task. In this case, the startup began with a little 12 megawatt gas generator in Southampton, New York. That's about the capacity of four wind turbines, but it was enough to get power plants in Long Island back online, which were able to power up all of New York City, eventually returning service to all those 30,000,000 people. The grid is a little bit of a house of cards. It's not necessarily flimsy, but if the whole thing gets knocked down, you have to rebuild it one card at a time and from the ground up. Restoring power after a major blackout is one of the most high stakes operations you can imagine. The consequences of messing it up are enormous,
cues.zh: 失去供电。为这么多人恢复供电绝非易事。这次恢复从一个位于纽约州南安普顿的12兆瓦小型燃气发电机开始。这大概相当于四台风力发电机的容量，但足以让长岛的发电厂重新上线，进而为整个纽约市供电，最终让那3000万人全部恢复用电。电网有点像纸牌屋。它未必脆弱，可一旦整个结构被推倒，你就得从地基开始，一张牌一张牌地重建。大停电后恢复供电，是你所能想象的风险最高的操作之一。搞砸的后果极其严重，

cues.en: but there's no way to practice a real life scenario.
cues.zh: 但你又没办法演练真实场景。

cues.en: It seems as simple as flipping a switch, but restoring power is more complicated than you might think. And, I built a model power grid here in the studio to show you how this works. This is my last video in a deep dive series on widespread
cues.zh: 看起来就像拨个开关那么简单，但恢复供电比你想的要复杂得多。我在演播室里搭了一个电网模型，来给你演示它是怎么运作的。这是我关于大范围

cues.en: outages to the power grid, so go back and check out those other videos if you want to learn more. I'm Grady, and this is Practical Engineering. In today's episode, we're talking about black starts on the grid.
cues.zh: 电网停电深度系列视频的最后一期，想了解更多就回去看看之前的那些视频。我是Grady，这里是Practical Engineering。今天这期，我们聊聊电网的黑启动。

cues.en: This video is sponsored by HelloFresh.
cues.zh: 本视频由 HelloFresh 赞助。

cues.en: More on them later.
cues.zh: 稍后再详细介绍。

cues.en: An ideal grid keeps running indefinitely.
cues.zh: 理想的电网会无限期持续运行。

cues.en: Maybe it sustains localized damage from lightning strikes, vehicle accidents, hurricanes, floods, and wayward squirrels,
cues.zh: 也许它会因雷击、车辆事故、飓风、洪水以及乱窜的松鼠而遭受局部损坏，

cues.en: but the protective devices trigger circuit breakers to isolate those faults and keep them from disrupting the rest of the system.
cues.zh: 但保护装置会触发断路器，隔离这些故障，防止它们影响系统其余部分。

cues.en: But, we know that no grid is perfect, and occasionally,
cues.zh: 但我们知道，没有电网是完美的，偶尔，

cues.en: the damage lines up just right or protective devices behave in unexpected ways that cascade into a widespread outage.
cues.zh: 损坏恰好凑在一起，或者保护装置出现意外行为，级联导致大范围停电。

cues.en: I sometimes use the word blackout kind of freely to refer to any amount of electrical service disruption, but it's really meant to describe an event like this, a widespread outage across most or all of an interconnected area.
cues.zh: 我有时会随意使用 blackout 这个词，来指任何程度的供电中断，但它真正描述的是这样的事件：一个互联区域的大部分或全部发生大范围停电。

cues.en: Lots of engineering,
cues.zh: 大量的工程投入，

cues.en: dedicated service from line workers, plenty of lessons learned from past mishaps,
cues.zh: 线路工人的敬业奉献，从过去事故中吸取的诸多教训，

cues.en: and a little bit of good fortune have all meant that we don't see too many true blackouts these days, but they still happen, and they're still a grid operator's worst nightmare.
cues.zh: 再加上一点好运气，都意味着如今我们很少见到真正的大停电，但它们仍会发生，而且仍是电网运营商最可怕的噩梦。

cues.en: We explored the extreme consequences
cues.zh: 我们探讨过极端后果

cues.en: that come from a large scale blackout in a previous video. With those consequences in mind, the task of bringing a power grid back online from nothing, called a black start, is frightfully
cues.zh: 这些后果来自之前视频中的大规模停电。考虑到这些后果，从零开始让电网恢复运行的任务——称为黑启动——极其

cues.en: consequential,
cues.zh: 严重，

cues.en: with significant repercussions if things go wrong. The main reason why black starts are so complicated is that it takes power to make power. Most large scale generating plants, from coal power to gas power to nuclear, need a fair amount of electricity just to operate. That sounds counterintuitive,
cues.zh: 一旦出错，会带来重大后果。黑启动如此复杂的主要原因在于，发电本身也需要用电。大多数大型发电厂，从煤电、气电到核电，仅运行就需要相当多的电力。这听起来有悖直觉，

cues.en: and, of course, configurations and equipment vary from plant to plant, but power generating stations are enormous industrial facilities.
cues.zh: 当然，各电厂的配置和设备各不相同，但发电站是庞大的工业设施。

cues.en: They have blowers and scrubbers, precipitators and reactors,
cues.zh: 它们有鼓风机、洗涤器、除尘器和反应器，

cues.en: compressors, computers, lights, coffee makers, control panels, and pumps, so many pumps.
cues.zh: 压缩机、电脑、照明、咖啡机、控制面板，还有泵，非常多的泵。

cues.en: Lubrication pumps, fuel pumps, feed water pumps, cooling water pumps, and much much more. Most of this equipment is both necessary for the plant to run and requires electricity.
cues.zh: 润滑油泵、燃料泵、给水泵、冷却水泵，还有更多更多。这些设备大多既是电厂运行所必需的，又都需要用电。

cues.en: Even the generators themselves need electricity to operate.
cues.zh: 甚至连发电机本身也需要用电才能运行。

cues.en: I don't own a grid scale three phase generator yet, but I do have an alternator for a pickup truck, and they are remarkably similar devices.
cues.zh: 我还没有电网级的三相发电机，但我有一台皮卡用的交流发电机，而它们是非常相似的设备。

cues.en: You probably already know that moving a conductor through a magnetic field generates a current. This physical phenomenon,
cues.zh: 你可能已经知道，让导体在磁场中运动就会产生电流。这个物理现象，

cues.en: called induction,
cues.zh: 叫做电磁感应，

cues.en: is the basis for almost all electricity
cues.zh: 是几乎所有电力的基础，

cues.en: generation on the grid. Some source of motion we call the prime mover, often a steam powered turbine, spins a shaft called a rotor inside a set of coils. But, you won't see a magnet on the rotor of a grid scale generator just like if you look closely inside the case, you won't see a magnet inside my alternator. You just see another winding of copper wire. Turns out that this physical phenomenon works both ways. If you put a current through a coil of wire, you get a magnetic field. If that coil is on a rotor, you can spin it like so.
cues.zh: 也就是电网上的发电。我们称某种运动来源为原动机，通常是蒸汽驱动的汽轮机，它带动一根叫转子的轴在一组线圈内旋转。但是，在电网级发电机的转子上你看不到磁铁；同样，如果你仔细看我的交流发电机内部，也看不到磁铁。你只会看到另一组铜线绕组。原来这个物理现象反过来也成立。让电流通过线圈，就会产生磁场。如果这个线圈在转子上，你就可以像这样把它转起来。

cues.en: This is my model power plant. I got this idea from a video by Bellingham Technical College, but their model was a little more sophisticated than mine. Let me give you a tour. On the right, we have the prime mover. Don't worry about the fact that it's an electric motor. My model power plant consumes more energy than it creates, but I didn't want to build a mini steam turbine just for this demonstration.
cues.zh: 这是我的模型电厂。这个想法来自 Bellingham Technical College 的一个视频，不过他们的模型比我的更精细一些。让我带你参观一下。右边是原动机。别在意它其实是一台电动机。我的模型电厂消耗的能量比产生的多，但我不想只为这次演示造一台迷你汽轮机。

cues.en: The thing that's important is that the prime mover drives a three phase generator,
cues.zh: 重点在于原动机驱动着一台三相发电机，

cues.en: in my case, through this belt. And, the generator you already saw is a car alternator that I modified
cues.zh: 在我这里是通过这根皮带驱动的。你们刚才看到的发电机其实是我改装的汽车交流发电机，

cues.en: to create an alternating current instead of a direct current like what's used in a vehicle. The alternator is connected to some resistors that simulate loads on the grid.
cues.zh: 让它输出交流电，而不是车载的那种直流电。发电机连接了一些电阻，用来模拟电网负载。

cues.en: And I have an oscilloscope hooked up to one of the phases so we can see the AC waveform.
cues.zh: 我还把一台示波器接在其中一相上，这样就能看到交流波形。

cues.en: Yeah. All this is so we could just see that sine wave on the oscilloscope.
cues.zh: 没错，搞这么大阵仗，就是为了在示波器上看到那个正弦波。

cues.en: It could have been a couple of tiny three phase motors. It could have even just been a signal generator.
cues.zh: 其实用几个微型三相电机就行，甚至直接用一台信号发生器也可以。

cues.en: But, you guys love these models, so I thought you deserved something slightly grander in scale. There's a few other things here too, including a second model power plant, but we'll get to those in a minute. The alternator I used in my model has two brushes of graphite that ride along the rotor so that we can supply current to the coil inside to create an electromagnet.
cues.zh: 但既然大家喜欢看模型，我就觉得应该搞个规模稍大一点的。这里还有其他一些东西，包括第二个模型发电厂，待会儿再讲。我模型里用的发电机有两个石墨电刷接触转子，这样就能给内部线圈通电形成电磁铁。

cues.en: This is called excitation,
cues.zh: 这叫做励磁，

cues.en: and it has a major benefit over using permanent magnets in a generator. It's adjustable.
cues.zh: 相比在发电机中使用永磁体，它有个巨大的优势：输出是可调节的。

cues.en: Let's power up the prime mover to see how it works. If there's no excitation current, there's no magnetic field, which means there's no power. We're just spinning two inert coils of wire right next to each other. But watch what happens when I apply some current to the brushes.
cues.zh: 我们启动原动机看看效果。如果没有励磁电流就没有磁场，也就意味着没有电能产生。我们只是让两个毫无反应的线圈挨着空转而已。但注意看，当我给电刷通上电流时会发生什么。

cues.en: Now, the rotor is excited, and I have to say, I'm pretty excited too, because I can see that we're generating power. As I increase the excitation current, we can see that the voltage across the resistor is higher, so we're generating more power. Of course, this additional power doesn't come for free. It also puts more and more mechanical load on the prime mover.
cues.zh: 现在，转子已经励磁了，而我得说，我也很兴奋，因为我能看到我们正在发电。随着我增大励磁电流，可以看到电阻两端的电压更高了，所以我们发的电更多了。当然，这些额外的电并不是白来的。它还会给原动机带来越来越大的机械负载。

cues.en: You can see when I spin the alternator with no excitation current, it turns freely, but when I increase the current, it becomes more difficult to spin.
cues.zh: 可以看到，当我在没有励磁电流的情况下转动交流发电机时，它转得很轻松；但当我增大电流时，它就越来越难转了。

cues.en: Modern power plants adjust the excitation current in a generator to regulate the voltage of electricity leaving the facility, something that would be much harder to do in a device that used permanent magnets that don't need electricity to create a magnetic field.
cues.zh: 现代电厂通过调节发电机的励磁电流，来调节电厂输出电力的电压；在使用永磁体的设备里，这会难得多，因为永磁体不需要用电来产生磁场。

cues.en: The power for the excitation system can come from the generator, but like the other equipment I mentioned, it can't start working until the plant is running. In fact, power plants often use around five to 10% of all the electricity they generate.
cues.zh: 励磁系统的电力可以来自发电机本身，但像我提到的其他设备一样，它要等电厂运行起来才能开始工作。事实上，电厂通常要消耗其总发电量的约 5% 到 10%。

cues.en: That's why a black start of a large power plant is often called bootstrapping
cues.zh: 这就是为什么大型电厂的黑启动常被称为“自举”

cues.en: because the facility has to pick itself up by the bootstraps.
cues.zh: 因为电厂必须靠自己的鞋带把自己提起来。

cues.en: It needs a significant amount of power both to start and maintain
cues.zh: 它需要大量电力，既用来启动，也用来维持

cues.en: its own creation of power, and that poses an obvious challenge. You might be familiar with the standby generators used at hospitals, cell phone towers, city water pumps, and many other critical facilities where a power outage could have severe consequences.
cues.zh: 自身的发电，而这带来了一个明显的挑战。你可能熟悉医院、手机信号塔、城市水泵以及许多其他关键设施里使用的备用发电机；在这些地方，停电可能造成严重后果。

cues.en: Lots of people even have small ones for their homes. These generators use diesel or natural gas for fuel and large banks of batteries to get started. Imagine the standby generator capacity that would be needed at a major power plant. 5% of the nearest plant to my house, even at a quarter of its nameplate capacity,
cues.zh: 很多人家里甚至备有小型发电机。这些发电机以柴油或天然气为燃料，并靠大型电池组启动。想象一下，一座大型电厂需要多么庞大的备用发电容量。离我家最近的电厂，哪怕只按其额定容量的四分之一算，其 5%

cues.en: is 18 megawatts.
cues.zh: 也有 18 兆瓦。

cues.en: That's more than a 100 of these.
cues.zh: 这相当于 100 多台这种发电机。

cues.en: It's just not feasible to maintain that amount of standby generation capacity at every power plant. Instead, we designate black start sources that can either spin up without support using batteries and standby devices or that can remain energized without a connection to the rest of the grid.
cues.zh: 在每座电厂都维持这种规模的备用发电容量根本不现实。因此，我们会指定一些黑启动电源，它们要么能靠电池和备用设备自行启动运转，要么在脱离电网其余部分时仍能保持带电。

cues.en: Obviously, these black power plants are more expensive to build and maintain, so we only have so many of them spread across each grid. Their combined capacity can only supply a small fraction of electricity demands,
cues.zh: 显然，这些黑启动电厂的建设和维护成本更高，所以每个电网中分布的数量非常有限。它们的总容量也只能满足极小一部分的用电需求，

cues.en: but we don't need them for that during a blackout. We just need them to create enough power so that larger baseload plants can spin up. Hydropower plants are often used as black start sources because they only need a little bit of electricity to open the gates and excite the generators to produce electricity.
cues.zh: 但在大停电期间，我们并不指望它们来全面供电。我们只需要它们提供足够的电能，让更大的基荷电厂运转起来。水电站经常被用作黑启动电源，因为它们只需要极少的电量来开启闸门并完成发电机励磁，就可以开始发电。

cues.en: Some wind turbines in solar plants could be used as black start sources, but most aren't set up for it because they don't produce power twenty four seven. But producing enough power to get the bigger plants started is only the first of many hurdles to restoring service during a blackout. The next step is to get the power to the plants.
cues.zh: 部分风力发电机和太阳能电站也可以用作黑启动电源，但大多数并没有为此配置，因为它们无法全天候 24 小时发电。然而，发出足够的电力来启动大型电厂，仅仅是大停电恢复供电过程中诸多难关的第一道。下一步，是要把电力输送到那些电厂。

cues.en: Luckily, we have some major extension cords stretched across the landscape.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，大地上延伸着一条条“超大号延长线”。

cues.en: We normally call them transmission lines, but during a blackout, they are cranking paths.
cues.zh: 平时我们称其为输电线路，但在大停电期间，它们叫作启动路径。

cues.en: That's because you can't just energize transmission lines with black start sources. First, those lines have to be isolated so that you don't inadvertently try to power up cities along the way. All the substations along a predetermined cranking path disconnect their transformers to isolate the transmission lines and create a direct route. Once the black start source starts up and energizes the cranking path, a baseload power plant can draw electricity directly from the line, allowing it to spin up. One trick to speed up recovery is to black start individual islands within the larger grid. That provides more flexibility and robustness in the process, but it creates a new challenge,
cues.zh: 这是因为你不能直接用黑启动电源为输电线路通电。首先必须隔离这些线路，以免不小心给沿途的城市送电。预定启动路径上的所有变电站都会断开它们的 Transformer 来隔离输电线路，从而开辟一条直连通道。一旦黑启动电源启动并为启动路径通电，基荷电厂就能直接从线路上取电并运转起来。加速恢复的一个技巧，是在大电网中对各个孤岛区域分别进行黑启动。这为整个过程提供了更高的灵活性和鲁棒性，但同时也带来了一个新挑战：

cues.en: synchronization.
cues.zh: 同步。

cues.en: Let's go back to the model to see how this works. I have both generating stations running now, each powering their own separate grid. This switch will connect the two together, but you can't just flip it willy nilly. Take a look at my oscilloscope, and it's easy to see that these two grids aren't synchronized.
cues.zh: 我们回到模型来看看这是如何运作的。现在两座发电站都在运行，各自为独立的电网供电。这个开关可以把两者连接起来，但你绝不能随便合闸。看看示波器，很容易发现这两个电网并没有同步。

cues.en: They're running at slightly different frequencies.
cues.zh: 它们的运行频率略有不同。

cues.en: If I just flip the switch when the voltage isn't equal between the two grids, there's a surge in current as the two generators mechanically synchronize.
cues.zh: 如果两座电网电压不相等时我直接合闸，两台发电机在进行机械同步的过程中就会产生瞬间的浪涌电流。

cues.en: We're only playing with a few volts here, so it's a little hard to see on camera. If I flip the switch when the two generators are out of sync, they jerk as the magnetic fields equalize their current.
cues.zh: 我们这里只玩几伏特的电压，所以在镜头上不太容易看清。当两台发电机不同步时，如果我合上开关，它们会猛地一颤，因为磁场会使电流趋于一致。

cues.en: If the difference is big enough, the two generators actually fight against each other, essentially trying to drive each other like motors.
cues.zh: 如果差异足够大，两台发电机实际上会互相较劲，本质上就像电动机一样互相驱动对方。

cues.en: It's kind of fun with this little model, but something like this in a real power plant would cause tremendous damage to equipment. So during a black start, each island, and in fact, each individual power plant that comes online, has to be perfectly synchronized.
cues.zh: 用这个小模型玩玩挺有意思，但如果这种事情发生在真实电厂里，会对设备造成巨大损坏。所以在黑启动过程中，每一个孤岛电网，实际上每一座接入电网的发电厂，都必须精确同步。

cues.en: And this is true outside of black star conditions as well. I can adjust the speed of my motors to get them spinning at nearly the exact same speed, then flip the switch when the waveforms match up just right. That prevents the surges of power between the two systems at the moment they're connected. You can see that the traces on the oscilloscope are identical now, showing that our two island grids are interconnected.
cues.zh: 这一原则在黑启动之外同样适用。我可以调整电机的转速，让它们以几乎完全相同的速度旋转，然后在波形刚好吻合的瞬间合上开关。这样就能避免两套系统在连接瞬间产生电力涌流。你可以看到示波器上的两条波形现在完全一致，表明我们的两个孤岛电网已经互联。

cues.en: One way to check this is to simply connect a light between the same phase on the two grids. If the light comes on, you know there's a difference in voltage between them and they aren't synchronized.
cues.zh: 一种检查方法是在两套电网的同一相之间接一个灯泡。如果灯亮了，说明两套电网之间存在电压差，还没有同步。

cues.en: If the light goes off and stays off, there's no voltage difference, meaning you're good to throw the breaker. Older plants were equipped with a synchroscope that would show both whether the plant was spinning at the same speed as the grid or faster or slower and whether the phase angle was a match. I bought an old one for this video, but it needs much higher voltages than I'm willing to play with in the studio, so let's just animate over the top of it. Operators would manually bring their generators up to speed, making slight adjustments to match the frequency of the rest of the grid. But matching the speed isn't enough, you also have to match the phase, so this was a careful dance. As soon as the syncroscope needle both stopped moving and was pointing directly up, the operator could close the breaker.
cues.zh: 如果灯灭了并且一直保持熄灭，说明没有电压差，这时就可以放心合上断路器了。老式电厂配有同步指示器，既能显示电厂转速是与电网相同还是偏快偏慢，也能显示相位角是否匹配。我为这期视频买了一台老式的，但它需要的工作电压远高于我愿意在演播室里摆弄的水平，所以我们就在它上面用动画来演示。操作员会手动把发电机提速到目标转速，稍作调整以匹配电网其余部分的频率。但仅仅转速匹配还不够，相位也必须匹配，所以这是一个需要小心翼翼的过程。一旦同步表的指针停止转动并且正好竖直朝上，操作员就可以合上断路器了。

cues.en: During a black start, utilities can start restoring power to their customers,
cues.zh: 在黑启动期间，电力公司可以开始恢复对用户的供电，

cues.en: slowly matching generation capacity with demand as more and more power plants come online.
cues.zh: 随着越来越多的电厂并网，逐步让发电容量与需求相匹配。

cues.en: Generally, the most critical loads will be prioritized
cues.zh: 通常，最关键负荷会被优先恢复，

cues.en: during the recovery, like natural gas infrastructure,
cues.zh: 在恢复过程中，比如天然气基础设施、

cues.en: communications,
cues.zh: 通信、

cues.en: hospitals, and military installations.
cues.zh: 医院和军事设施。

cues.en: But even connecting customers adds complexity to restoration.
cues.zh: 但即便只是给用户送电，也会增加恢复工作的复杂性。

cues.en: Some of our most power hungry appliances only get more hungry the longer they've been offline. For example, an outage during the summer means all the buildings are heating up with no access to air conditioning. When the power does come back on, it's not just a few air conditioners ready to run, it's all of them at once. Add to that refrigerators,
cues.zh: 我们一些最耗电的电器，断电时间越长反而越耗电。例如，夏季停电意味着所有建筑都在升温，却无法使用空调。等电力恢复时，不只是几台空调准备运行，而是所有空调同时启动。再加上冰箱、

cues.en: furnaces, freezers, and hot water heaters, and you can imagine the enormous initial demand on the grid after an extended outage. And, don't forget that many of these appliances use inductive motors that have huge inrush currents. For example, here's an ammeter on the motor of my table saw while I start it up. It draws a whopping 28 amps as it gets up to speed before settling down to four amps at no load. Imagine the demand from thousands of motors like this starting all at the exact same instant. The technical term for this is cold load pickup, and it could be as high as eight to 10 times normal electrical demands before the diversity of loads starts to average out again, usually after about thirty minutes. So, grid operators have to be very deliberate about how many customers they restore service to at a time.
cues.zh: 暖气炉、冰柜和热水器，你就能想象长时间停电后电网面临的巨大初始需求。还有，别忘了许多这类电器使用感应电机，启动涌流很大。比如，这是我启动台锯时电机上的电流表。它在加速到全速时电流高达 28 安培，空载稳定后才降到 4 安培。想象一下成千上万台这样的电机在同一瞬间启动带来的需求。这个技术术语叫冷负荷启动，在各类负荷的多样性重新拉平均需求之前，它可能高达正常用电需求的 8 到 10 倍，通常大约 30 分钟后才会趋于平均。所以，电网运营商必须非常谨慎地决定每次恢复多少用户的供电。

cues.en: If you ever see your neighbor a few blocks away getting power before you, keep in mind this delicate balancing act that operators have to perform in order to get the grid through the cold load pickup for each new group of customers that go online.
cues.zh: 如果你发现隔壁几个街区的邻居家比你先通电，请记住，调度人员必须完成极其微妙的平衡操作，才能让电网承受住每一批新用户接入时的冷负荷启动冲击。

cues.en: The ability to black start a power grid quickly after a total collapse is so important because electricity is vital to our health and safety. After the two thousand three blackout in The US, new reliability standards were issued including one that requires grid operators to have detailed system restoration plans. That includes maintaining black start sources even though it's often incredibly expensive.
cues.zh: 在电网彻底瘫痪后迅速进行黑启动的能力至关重要，因为电力直接关乎我们的健康与安全。2003 年美国大停电后，相关部门出台了新的可靠性标准，其中一项就要求电网运营商必须制定详尽的系统恢复方案。这包括维护黑启动电源，尽管其成本往往极其高昂。

cues.en: Some standby equipment mostly just does that, stands by, but it still has to be carefully maintained and regularly tested in the rare case that it gets called into service.
cues.zh: 有些备用设备绝大部分时间就只是在那儿“备着”，但即便极少被调用，依然必须精心维护并定期测试，以备不时之需。

cues.en: Also, the grid is incredibly vulnerable during a black start, and if something goes wrong, breakers can trip and you might have to start all over again. Utilities have strict security measures to try and ensure that no one could intentionally
cues.zh: 此外，电网在黑启动期间极其脆弱，一旦出现差错，断路器就可能跳闸，导致一切不得不从头再来。电力公司采取了严格的安保措施，力求确保没有人能蓄意

cues.en: disable or frustrate the black start process.
cues.zh: 破坏或阻碍黑启动过程。

cues.en: Finally, they do detailed analysis to make sure they can bring their grid up from scratch, including testing and even running drills to practice the procedures.
cues.zh: 最后，他们还会进行详尽的分析，确保电网能从零恢复，包括开展各项测试，甚至组织实战演练来熟悉整套流程。

cues.en: All this cost and effort and careful engineering
cues.zh: 付出这一切成本、心血和精密的工程设计，

cues.en: just to ensure that we can get the grid back up and running to power homes and businesses after a major blackout.
cues.zh: 都只是为了确保在严重大停电之后，我们能让电网重新运转起来，为千家万户和工商业恢复供电。
